description: Hi, I'm Advay, a student dev (Python/JS/HTML/CSS/AI). Team Firelytics AI is tackling 'Flame in Freefall': an AI dashboard summarizing, ranking, and interpreting NASA microgravity combustion data to improve fire safety for space missions. We need a data analyst (Pandas/ML), frontend/UI dev, and a microgravity/combustion science expert. If interested, join us! Beginners welcome. Please include your skills in your request!

details:
Firelytics AI — Project Details

What the project does

Firelytics AI is a research-support app for exploring NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) investigations related to combustion in microgravity. It combines a web interface, a FastAPI backend, and a local SQLite database. The supplied database contains 26 investigations, with report text indexed for 15. The app also has an 11-investigation fallback catalogue for use when the backend is unavailable; neither catalogue represents all of NASA PSI.

Users can browse and filter investigations, search with natural-language questions, view metadata, compare studies, and ask for AI-assisted explanations. For details that are not in the metadata, users can manually download a source file from PSI and upload it for analysis. Uploaded files are extracted for the session and are not permanently stored by the upload endpoint.

 How it works

The database pipeline parses PSI investigation metadata, extracts text from PDFs, creates CSV and JSON catalogues, and builds an SQLite database with an FTS5 full-text search index.

For AI-assisted search, Groq can convert a user’s question into scientific search concepts. SQLite FTS5 then finds and ranks matching investigations. If Groq is unavailable or not configured, search can use a lexical fallback.

For explanations and comparisons, the backend sends available investigation metadata—and relevant user-uploaded file contents, if provided—to the configured analysis model. It is instructed to distinguish source information from interpretation and not to invent missing results. PSI file-manifest discovery is present for investigation sessions, but automatic file downloads and extraction through the session endpoints are currently disabled.

Benefits and intended impact

The app brings investigation metadata and indexed report text into one searchable workspace. It can help researchers locate relevant studies, understand their stated objectives and methods, and compare investigations more easily by uploading their own report files. By making source links and evidence limitations visible, it aims to support research that may inform spacecraft fire-safety work. It does not make verified safety decisions.

Tools and technologies

- Frontend: JavaScript, React, Vite, and Lucide icons.

- Backend: Python and FastAPI, with Pydantic request models.

- Database and search: SQLite and FTS5.

- AI integration: Groq API when configured; lexical fallback is available for search.

- File processing: Python libraries for PDF, spreadsheet, document, and presentation extraction.

- Hardware: No dedicated development hardware is documented. The app was created and tested directly on local machines.

What is creative about the approach

The project combines structured scientific records, full-text search, and AI-assisted explanations in one research workflow. It also lets a researcher add a source file manually to a temporary investigation session when metadata alone does not answer a question. The system keeps uploaded evidence associated with its selected investigation and distinguishes metadata-based explanations from file-based analysis.

Factors considered

- The local catalogue is a subset, not a complete mirror of NASA PSI.

- “Not listed in the supplied inventory” does not mean “confirmed absent from NASA PSI.”

- Metadata availability does not prove that analyzed measurements are available.

- Some files may not be extractable; scanned PDFs need OCR, which is not implemented.

- Uploaded evidence is temporary and subject to file-size and format limits.

- AI output must not invent measurements, findings, or citations.

- Firelytics AI is a research-support prototype, not an operational safety system.
